title: Inference CI: smoke-runner notes
content:
Goal: lightweight, automatable inference smoke runner that exercises latency/cost/quality on PRs and flags regressions before merge. Not a full eval rig — minimal, fast, deterministic checks that catch common breakages (kernel changes, batching regressions, KV cache regressions, model fallback behavior).

Why we need it
- We deploy fast; small changes in kernels/configs can silently increase p50/p95 or token-cost.
- Evals take too long and are noisy for PR feedback. Need quick guard rails integrated into developer flow.
- Reduce post-merge incident surface and speed up safe rollouts.

MVP hypothesis
- A 3–5 test scenario runner that completes in < 3min per PR and gives deterministic p50/p95 latency, token-cost delta, and a quality sanity score (embedding similarity or exact-match where appropriate). If any metric crosses a threshold, fail CI check.

User stories
- As an infra engineer, I want a CI check to catch regressions in request throughput and latency before merging changes to serving runtime.
- As an SDK owner, I want to know if a PR causes increased token usage (e.g., formatting changes in streaming) so I can fix it early.
- As SRE, I want artifacts (request traces, small flamegraphs, model outputs) attached to the PR to triage quickly.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- GitHub check named "Inference Smoke Runner" returns pass/fail on PRs to main branches.
- Runner executes 4 canonical scenarios: short chat reply (low tokens), long completion (100–300 tokens), streaming path, embedding call.
- Each scenario records p50/p95 latency, token usage, and one quality metric (embedding cosine > baseline - 0.02 or exact-match % > X).
- Baselines stored in small JSON in repo. CI fails when p95 increases by > 20% or token usage increases by > 15% or quality drops below threshold.
- Artifacts uploaded to a deterministic S3 prefix and link attached to PR check.

Design notes — runner architecture
- Lightweight container (runner) executed as GitHub Action or CircleCI job. Container needs ephemeral credentials that point to a sandboxed test account (restricted quota).
- Runner supports two execution modes: hosted-sandbox (calls Redwood hosted API using sandbox key) and local-emulator (containerized tiny runtime for offline PRs). Default is hosted-sandbox for end-to-end realism.
- Each scenario has: input (prompt + optional partial context), model identifier (can be pinned to a small known model), runtime config (batch size, concurrency, quantization flag), expected baseline artifact. Runner executes N=3 runs per scenario to smooth variance.
- Metrics collection: p50/p95 latency (client-observed), request/response token counts, model returned text, embedding vectors. Minimal tracing context (request id + route) included.
- Quality checks: small suite of deterministic assertions per scenario and an embedding-similarity fallback. Use fixed seeds and fixed instructions to reduce nondeterminism.

Baseline management
- Baselines stored as small YAML/JSON in repo under /ci/inference-baselines. Baselines include: baseline_latency_ms (p50/p95), baseline_tokens, baseline_embedding_vector (serialized float32 base64 or small fingerprint hash), baseline_output_snippets.
- Baseline bumps must be approved via a dedicated PR with a short changelist explaining why. Hooks to require owner approval for baseline updates.

Failure modes and noise handling
- Variance from network/infrastructure: mitigate with multiple runs and require sustained regressions (e.g., two consecutive PR runs failing) before enforcing stricter gating.
- Non-deterministic model outputs: prefer embedding similarity for semantics and simple exact-match where deterministic. Add optional fuzzy thresholds.
- Rate limiting or throttling on hosted sandbox: monitor quota and fallback to local-emulator in degraded mode.

Security / cost considerations
- Use a special restricted sandbox API key with strict rate limits and no production data access. Keys to rotate and be stored in secret manager.
- Cap number of runs per PR and provide a credit budget. Default N=3 runs * 4 scenarios should be cheap. Track costs in a daily budget alert.

Observability + triage artifacts
- Upload: request/response JSON (redacted PII), small flamegraph images for top kernels (if available), raw embedding vectors, and a summary CSV of measured metrics.
- PR check attaches a short JSON summary and link to artifacts. Include a generated short explanation: e.g., "p95 increased 38% (baseline 120ms -> 165ms) on long completion; token increase +12%; quality unchanged."

Integration with developer workflow
- GitHub Action template provided. Running locally via `./tools/inference-ci --local` for dev runs.
- Slack/PR bot to ping owners on failures and to annotate a failure reason with suggested hot paths.

MVP implementation plan (2 sprints)
- Sprint 1: minimal runner container, 4 scenarios, GitHub Action wiring, baseline JSON, artifact upload to test S3, fail/pass checks. Owner: Mika Sato.
- Sprint 2: embed quality checks, local-emulator mode, artifact links in PR, baseline bump workflow. Owner: Aditya Kapoor + Noah Garcia.

Follow-ups / Nice-to-haves
- Canary gating: auto-block merge only on changes to serving runtime or model packaging PRs; for other repos run but warn.
- Auto-bisecter: when a PR fails, try to point to the earliest commit (in a window) that introduced regression.
- Visual diff UI in Console showing side-by-side latency and token deltas for recent commits.
- Bench-mode: scheduled nightly runs across models/regions to detect slow drift.

Risks / open questions
- Will hosted-sandbox variability make this noisy and cause developer friction? Need to pilot with subset of team first.
- Who owns maintenance and baseline drift approval? Suggest shared ownership between eng-serving-runtime and platform team.
- Should the runner attempt to replicate different hardware (A100 vs T4) behavior? Initially no, stick to a single canonical test region/hardware.

Quick TODO (next 7 days)
- Spike: build a minimal container that runs a single long-completion scenario against hosted sandbox and returns p95 + token count. (Owner: Aditya)
- Create /ci/inference-baselines initial JSON with 4 scenarios. (Owner: Mika)
- Create GH Action skeleton and attach to a test repo. (Owner: Tess)
- Add secret rotation plan and request sandbox API key from infra. (Owner: Noah)

Notes to self / small heuristics
- Keep scenarios small and deterministic; any test that takes >3 minutes is too long.
- Prefer p95 and token delta thresholds over p50 for gating.
- Track false positives for 2 weeks and relax thresholds if many noise-driven fails.

References / inspiration
- internal: prompt-unit-test-harness (see /repos/internal/prompt-tests)
- external: "ai-ci" patterns, ML model regression checks (e.g., Hugging Face CI examples)

End of notes — rough sketch. Will flesh into PRD if spike proves feasibility.
